verdict.rationale: Cal.com's own docs say it offers "an embed flow" and embeddable React components (Cal Atoms) for adding scheduling to your app. A Framer integration also adds Cal.com to websites. However, the evidence never describes inline, popup, or floating-widget modes, and never shows a copy-paste embed snippet. missing for 10: documented inline/popup/floating-button embed modes, a published embed snippet or code example, independent or hands-on corroboration of embedding.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed the booking experience in my own site — inline, popup, or floating widget — with a documented snippet

citations.quote: Cal.com offers a v2 REST API, embeddable React components (Cal Atoms), an embed flow, and a hosted MCP server for AI agents.
Use our react atoms to add scheduling to your app
Find out how to use Cal "atoms" to integrate scheduling into your product.
Add Cal.com to Framer, the design tool for websites.
